reason: A Connectivity Map build-02 compound code (the DSigDB sets are MCF7/PC3 up/down signatures). Neither ChEMBL (pref_name, synonym and free-text search all empty) nor PubChem (compound and substance name lookups return nothing) has a record under this code. It cannot be mapped without guessing.

This is the CAS index name of brefeldin A (C16H24O4), given without stereodescriptors. PubChem resolves it to Brefeldin A (CID 5287620) and to CID 5351204, which carries this name as its title plus the synonym 'BFA' and brefeldin NSC numbers. DSigDB has no separate 'Brefeldin A' entry, so this CTD set is brefeldin A. ChEMBL CHEMBL19980 BREFELDIN A matches InChIKey KQNZDYYTLMIZCT-KQPMLPITSA-N and is its own parent. The old first hit, CHEMBL2402356 (C17H24O5, an acetyl analogue), was wrong. CHEMBL1734306 is the epimer from PubChem's title record. Both have a null phase, so the choice does not change the ranking.

This is a PAH pollutant with no ChEMBL pref_name. PubChem CID 13257 has InChIKey DOWJXOHBNXRUOD-UHFFFAOYSA-N, and it matches exactly one ChEMBL record: CHEMBL3561957 (SMILES Cc1cccc2c1ccc1ccccc12, methyl at C1). It is its own parent and has a null phase. The old first hit, CHEMBL403878 (C18H18O3, a trimethoxy-methylphenanthrene), was wrong. The search hit CHEMBL1797288 is 2-methylphenanthrene, not this compound.

The exact rule missed this only because of a space ('Naphthyl isothiocyanate' vs 'NAPHTHYLISOTHIOCYANATE'). PubChem CID 11080 has InChIKey JBDOSUUXMYMWQH-UHFFFAOYSA-N, which matches only CHEMBL1381098. It is its own parent and has a null phase. The old first hit was correct.

This is PCB 180 (PubChem CID 37036, InChIKey WBHQEUPUMONIKF-UHFFFAOYSA-N). The InChIKey and a SMILES flexmatch both return only CHEMBL375479. Its SMILES has chlorines at 2,3,4,5 on one ring and 2',4',5' on the other. It has no pref_name, is its own parent and has a null phase.

'2E,4E,6E,8E' is a parsing fragment. The only DSigDB term containing it is '(2E,4E,6E,8E)-3,7-DIMETHYL-9-(2,6,6-TRIMETHYL-3-OXO-1-CYCLOHEXENYL)NONA-2,4,6,8-TETRAENOIC ACID CTD 00000070'. PubChem resolves that full name to 4-oxoretinoic acid (CID 6437063, InChIKey GGCUJPCCTQNTJF-FRCNGJHJSA-N), which matches only ChEMBL CHEMBL104049. It is its own parent and has a null phase. This is medium, not high, confidence because it depends on decoding the fragment through the DSigDB source row. The fragment alone names no substance. Ranking pipelines should check that this row's gene set is that CTD term.

3-Amino-1,2,4-triazole is amitrole (PubChem CID 1639, InChIKey KLSJWNVTNUYHDU-UHFFFAOYSA-N). That key matches only CHEMBL232801 AMITROLE (SMILES Nc1nc[nH]n1). It is its own parent and has a null phase. The old first hit, CHEMBL15571 (1,2,4-triazole, which lacks the amino group), was wrong.

4-Oxoretinol is PubChem CID 5289090 (C20H28O2, InChIKey PLIUCYCUYQIBDZ-RMWYGNQTSA-N). ChEMBL has no record for the full InChIKey or its connectivity block. A SMILES flexmatch finds nothing, and the only hit at 80% similarity is canthaxanthin. No pref_name or synonym matches either. The old first hit, elosulfase alfa (CHEMBL2108676, phase 4, an enzyme), was wrong and would have wrongly admitted it. Retinol (CHEMBL986) is a different compound.

5-Aminosalicylic acid is mesalamine. CHEMBL704 MESALAMINE (SMILES Nc1ccc(O)c(C(=O)O)c1) is its own parent and is phase 4. Do not confuse it with CHEMBL1169 AMINOSALICYLIC ACID, which is 4-aminosalicylic acid (PAS). The old first hit was correct. The exact rule missed it because ChEMBL does not list this spelling as a synonym.

6-Thioguanine is thioguanine. CHEMBL727 THIOGUANINE (SMILES Nc1nc2[nH]cnc2c(=S)[nH]1) is its own parent and is phase 4. The old first hit was correct. The exact rule missed it because the '6-' spelling is not a ChEMBL synonym.

It is its own parent and has max_phase 1.0, so it now passes the phase 1-4 filter. The old first hit, CHEMBL5796501 (an unnamed nitrile peptidomimetic), was wrong.

The rule left this unresolved, but ChEMBL does have the exact substance. It is its own parent and has no phase.

The second reviewer is right. The bare code is not a ChEMBL name or synonym, and free-text search returns 0. But the identity does not come from a similar name. PubChem's substance index maps source ChemBridge, id 5109870, to SID 442840067 and then to CID 135409239, which is C13H13N3O2, 2-methoxy-6-[(pyridin-2-ylhydrazinylidene)methyl]phenol. Sci Rep 6:38343 (PMC5141479, a Connectivity Map iron-chelator study) names 'The ChemBridge compound 5109870 (2-hydroxy-3-methoxybenzaldehyde 2-pyridinylhydrazone)'. ChEMBL has exactly one record with this connectivity (InChIKey prefix FFZWBZJRENXDNU, total_count 1): CHEMBL3350760. Its compound record name is '2-hydroxy-3-methoxybenzaldehyde 2-pyridinylhydrazone', it has no pref_name, it is its own parent, and max_phase is null. The only difference is that ChEMBL draws the E hydrazone and PubChem's ChemBridge deposit draws Z. Same constitution, formula and name, so it is one substance drawn two ways. This makes it the exact record the policy asks for. The phase is null, so the row is still dropped by the phase 1-4 filter.

The second reviewer is right. Exact pref_name and synonym searches for 'Sodium dichromate' do return 0, but ChEMBL does hold the exact substance under no name. A formula query for Cr2Na2O7 returns one record, CHEMBL3991158: small molecule, structure_type NONE, no synonyms, max_phase null. Separately, CHEMBL1477585 (H4Cr2Na2O9) has Tox21/NCGC compound records SID17388732, SID17388733, SID144204729 and SID144209734. PubChem gives all four as 'Sodium dichromate dihydrate', CAS 7789-12-0. Its molecule_hierarchy parent_chembl_id is CHEMBL3991158. So the named hydrate is parented to the anhydrous Na2Cr2O7 record, and no other substance has that formula. That makes it the exact substance named, not another salt that merely contains chromium, as potassium dichromate CHEMBL1374101 and the acid DICHROMATE CHEMBL1697701 are. The policy's 'exact substance' condition is met. max_phase is null, so the phase filter still drops it.
